concepts.definition: Standard units used to measure weight (kg, gm, mg) and capacity (l, ml, kl).
A part of a whole, written as numerator/denominator.
A fraction where the numerator and denominator have no common factors other than 1.

tasks.title: Task 1: Convert the following units of measurement.

questions.question: **4** kg = ___ gm
questions.hint: 1 kg = 1000 gm. Multiply the number of kilograms by 1000.

questions.question: **12000** mg = ___ gm
questions.hint: 1000 mg = 1 gm. Divide the number of milligrams by 1000.

questions.question: **10000** gm = ___ kg
questions.hint: 1000 gm = 1 kg. Divide the number of grams by 1000.

questions.question: **3** kg = ___ mg
questions.hint: 1 kg = 1000 gm and 1 gm = 1000 mg. Multiply kilograms by 1,000,000.

questions.question: **10** gm = ___ mg
questions.hint: 1 gm = 1000 mg. Multiply the number of grams by 1000.

questions.question: **5** l = ___ ml
questions.hint: 1 l = 1000 ml. Multiply the number of litres by 1000.

questions.question: **1000** ml = ___ l
questions.hint: 1000 ml = 1 l. Divide the number of millilitres by 1000.

questions.question: **13** l = ___ ml
questions.hint: 1 l = 1000 ml. Multiply the number of litres by 1000.

questions.question: **15000** ml = ___ l
questions.hint: 1000 ml = 1 l. Divide the number of millilitres by 1000.

questions.question: **2000** l = ___ kl
questions.hint: 1000 l = 1 kl. Divide the number of litres by 1000.

tasks.title: Task 2: Reduce the fractions to their lowest terms.

questions.question: Reduce **30/45** to its lowest terms.
questions.hint: Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 30 and 45. Divide both numerator and denominator by the GCD.

questions.question: Reduce **18/24** to its lowest terms.
questions.hint: Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 18 and 24. Divide both numerator and denominator by the GCD.

questions.question: Reduce **14/28** to its lowest terms.
questions.hint: Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 14 and 28. Divide both numerator and denominator by the GCD.

questions.question: Reduce **20/50** to its lowest terms.
questions.hint: Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 20 and 50. Divide both numerator and denominator by the GCD.

questions.question: **40 l 300 ml** + **12 l 985 ml** = ___ l ___ ml
questions.hint: Add litres and millilitres separately. If millilitres exceed 1000, convert to litres.

questions.question: **21200 ml** - **11300 ml** = ___ ml
questions.hint: Subtract the two quantities directly.

tasks.title: Task 4: Compare fractions with < or > or = in the box.

questions.hint: Compare the numerators when denominators are the same. The larger numerator means a larger fraction.
questions.solution: Both fractions have the same denominator (8). 7 > 6, so 7/8 > 6/8.

questions.hint: Compare the numerators when denominators are the same. The larger numerator means a larger fraction.
questions.solution: Both fractions have the same denominator (8). 1 < 9, so 1/8 < 9/8.

questions.hint: Compare the numerators when denominators are the same. The larger numerator means a larger fraction.
questions.solution: Both fractions have the same denominator (12). 1 < 7, so 1/12 < 7/12.

tasks.title: Task 5: Application of measurement in real situations.

questions.question: A can of **14 l** of oil was purchased for an event. After the event, **6 l 325 ml** of oil was left in the can. How much oil was used for the event?
questions.hint: Subtract the remaining oil from the total oil purchased. Convert litres to millilitres if needed.

questions.question: A bottle of juice holds **900 ml** of juice. Can three such bottles be poured into a jar of **2900 l**? Explain your answer with proper reasoning and show your thinking in the workspace provided.
questions.answer: Yes, three bottles can be poured into the jar. Total juice from three bottles is 2700 ml (2.7 l), which is less than 2900 l.
questions.hint: Calculate the total juice from three bottles and compare it to the jar's capacity. Remember 1000 ml = 1 l.
questions.solution: One bottle = 900 ml. Three bottles = 900 ml × 3 = 2700 ml = 2.7 l. The jar holds 2900 l, which is much larger than 2.7 l. So, yes, three bottles can be poured into the jar.
